classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish coincident lines from distinct parallel lines when a parameter controls the gradient.

content.prompt: The equations of two lines are $mx+y=2$ and $2x+5y=10$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: For what values of $m$ will the two lines not intersect?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-mx+2\\2x+5y&=10\\y&=-\frac25x+2\end{align*}$$
Both lines pass through $(0,2)$ for every $m$, so they always have a common point. There is no value of $m$ for which they do not intersect.

children.label: b
children.prompt: For what values of $m$ will the two lines intersect?

answer.worked:
Substitute $(0,2)$ into both equations:
$$\begin{align*}m(0)+2&=2\\2(0)+5(2)&=10\end{align*}$$
Thus $(0,2)$ lies on both lines for every $m$, so they intersect for any $m$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: For the values of $m$ found in part b, comment on the intersection of the lines.

answer.short: If $m=\frac25$, the lines coincide. Otherwise, they intersect at $(0,2)$.
answer.worked:
The gradient forms are $y=-mx+2$ and $y=-\frac25x+2$. Their gradients are equal when
$$\begin{align*}-m&=-\frac25\\m&=\frac25.\end{align*}$$
When $m=\frac25$, both equations represent the same line, so there are infinitely many common points. When $m\ne\frac25$, the gradients differ and the lines intersect only at $(0,2)$.
